rationale: Tests the fixed-ratio GOLD spirometric criterion for COPD diagnosis — the most frequently examined OAD fact
Tests understanding that hypercapnia in severe OAD results from ventilation-perfusion mismatch and respiratory muscle fatigue, not simply from low inspired oxygen
Tests the ability to identify the classical examination findings that distinguish emphysematous COPD ('pink puffer') from the chronic bronchitis phenotype
Tests the clinical pearl that absence of wheeze does not exclude severe asthma — a 'silent chest' is an ominous sign
Tests spirometric interpretation and GOLD severity staging based on post-bronchodilator FEV1% predicted
Tests that a chest X-ray can be normal in mild-to-moderate COPD and is not required for diagnosis
Tests GINA step-up therapy and the contraindication of LABA monotherapy in asthma
Tests the target oxygen saturation in COPD exacerbation to avoid suppression of hypoxic drive
Tests the 5As framework for smoking cessation counselling — specifically the correct sequence and content of each step
Tests understanding that nicotine dependence has both pharmacological and psychosocial components — relapse is not simply a failure of willpower
